title: Monolithic God Services
damaged_code:
```
/services/core_enterprise_service/
  - Handles customer signups
  - Manages payment processing
  - Generates financial tax reports
  - Dispatches truck shipments
  - Compiles marketing emails
```
pattern: Lumping unrelated functional domains and business workflows into a single massive distributed service ("The God Monolith").
why_bad: Forces coordinated deployments of the entire system for a minor change in any subdomain. If the tax calculator hits a memory leak, it crashes the payment processor and user signups. It limits independent scalability; developers cannot scale the high-traffic payment layer without scaling the heavy, low-frequency tax reporting layer.
detection: A single deployable service with endpoints and database models spanning multiple, completely unrelated business domains.
counterexample: Small startups or early-stage MVPs where a single deployment unit ("Monolith") is necessary to move fast before domain boundaries are discovered.
fix:
Extract unrelated business domains into independent services that coordinate through clear API boundaries.
```
/services/payment_service/
/services/shipping_service/
```
source: *Juval Löwy - Righting Software (2019)*, Chapter 2, "AVOID FUNCTIONAL DECOMPOSITION" (Lumping operations into mega services, p. 15); *Martin Kleppmann - Designing Data-Intensive Applications (2017)*, Chapter 1.
